output.explanation:
The central tree shrinks from 137 to 85 lines (38.0%) and from 10033 to 6299 characters (37.2%). It follows API responsibilities and handoffs rather than repeating four separate inventories. [M] marks modular boundaries, [C] calls, [O] ownership and lifetime, and [D] computational prerequisites. Five peripherals concentrate batching/replay, browser transport, live-reader validity, compact anchors, and saving/context mechanisms. Numeric limits and detailed cleanup live in peripherals. Seven connections attach to meaningful concepts; all diagrams are reachable. Measured text rectangles do not overlap, with at least 19 columns between neighboring columns and three rows between vertically adjacent trees. Rendered connector routing remains unverified.

Source-grounded corrections: diagram-context status uses binding presence and the current source fingerprint; materialization supplies the context payload separately (sessionService.ts:241-249). The checkpoint publication path applies when nodeId is absent; nodeId saving instead isolates a version-checked diagram, rebases metadata and exports history without canvas edges (sessionService.ts:672-714). QuickJS lifetime is one runtime invocation, including replay invocations, while the session service retains retry state (execRuntime.ts:5-27; sessionService.ts:333-562). Browser polling and selection publication have separate effect cleanup paths (useAgentCanvasBridge.ts:26-83).

Details beyond the seed include precise batch barriers and stable internal request prefixes, distinct transport and mutation identities, copy capability negotiation, whole-diagram selection constraints, socket feature gates, anchor capacity, jump-target membership checks and retained context-mutation payloads. These come from the eight pinned source texts.

The critique's navigation recommendation is applied using related point IDs explicitly supplied in context: editor, canvas, changes, generation and contexts. Other points are not reconstructed. The critique reports that runtime/central establishes projection sharing, but its underlying composition source is not pinned here. I therefore reject treating that report as verified implementation evidence: apiProjection.ts:10 states the sharing intention, while both service constructors permit injection and independently default to new instances. The remaining uncertainty concerns composition outside this point, not the demonstrated per-instance map behavior. Likewise, reported isolated-controller receipts elsewhere cannot establish deduplication for every live transport. This hook's command-ID cache alone cannot deduplicate a fresh dispatch ID. Only context.json and seed.json supply code evidence; the critique and previous output guide presentation, not factual claims.

Exec: batching and replay decisions
|-- Freeze each API step before dispatch [C/O]

|   |-- Step signature = method + args; changed replay fails

|-- Batched operations expose dependent IDs before application [C/D]

|   |-- Also flush before nodes.setSourceMappings and nodes.setJumps
|   |-- Batch retains step indices and expectedVersion; changed indices fail
|   `-- Applied batch updates version and invalidates cached nodes/edges
|-- Ambiguous transport outcomes keep the run retryable [O]
|   |-- Timeout, reply-too-large and reply-rejected preserve uncertain steps
|   |-- Retry invokes the script again and replays completed API outcomes
|   |-- Unfinished steps resend their retained operation and request identity
|   |-- Script-caught timeout still prevents reporting unfinished work as done
|   `-- Success or non-transport failure removes the execRuns entry
|-- Request-promise caching is separate from replay [O]
|   |-- Transport ambiguity removes the outer promise to admit another attempt
|   `-- Pure read release requires a version result with no transaction
|-- New document path [C]
|   |-- createDocument/copyDocument require unbound exec; one creation per run
|   `-- Copy attaches directly after reply, without waiting for descriptor refresh
`-- QuickJS bounds apply afresh to each runtime invocation [O]
    |-- 32 MiB memory; 512 KiB stack; at most 100 host API calls

    `-- Interrupt callback checks 30s deadline or more than 20000 interrupts

Browser dispatch: transport identity and retirement

|-- Dispatch and reply [C/O]

|   |-- At most 100 pending dispatches; polling waits up to 15s
|   |-- canvasId + commandId match settles the promise and clears its timer
|   `-- After 25s, reject and remove queued command; outcome can remain unknown
|-- Mutation retry identity crosses a different boundary [D]
|   |-- Exec payload preserves its request ID across fresh transport dispatches
|   `-- Hook cache alone cannot deduplicate a newly allocated command ID
`-- Retirement paths [O]

    |-- pagehide sends DELETE for this ephemeral instance

    `-- Selection publication uses a separate effect and cleanup

Live readers: selection validity and retained requests
|-- Reconstruct the next selection [D]
|   |-- Ignore same-epoch updates with sequence <= retained sequence
|   |-- Delta requires previous epoch and baseSequence to match
|   |-- Remove regions, then upsert; omitted diagramIds retains prior list

    |-- Short context GET sets no-store
